Gorilla targets $450M-$500M 2027 revenue while expecting Yotta 2 full deployment by February
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Gorilla Technology Group Inc. (GRRR) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Gorilla Technology has just delivered the largest revenue quarter in its history." (CEO & Executive Chairman Jayesh Chandan)

  • "In Q3, we delivered a record of $69.5 million." and "that is 163% growth year-on-year and almost 39% sequentially." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "The majority of our current revenue continues to come from these broader technology and infrastructure operations. GPU as a service remains relatively small contributor today." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "Since the end of September, we have received approximately over $22 million from Egypt with further collections of about $15 million to $17 million being pursued right now." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "We are doing with a Tier 1 investment bank a $1.7 billion bond is -- I would expect it to close within weeks." (Chief Financial Officer Bruce Bower)

Outlook

  • "Our minimum revenue outlook for 2026 remains at $200 million." and "our 2027 revenue target remains at $450 million to $500 million." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "For 2026, I mean, I would see the gross margin in the fourth quarter, improving sequentially but it wouldn't be a dramatic change." (CFO Bower)

  • "We will recognize some revenue from GPU as a service in the fourth quarter, but it won't be enough to dramatically shift the gross margins for the full year." (CFO Bower)

  • "The real impact from the improved gross margin from GPU as a service will come in the first quarter when the revenue numbers will become quite large and also the margin impact will be tremendous." (CFO Bower)

Financial Results

  • "In Q3, we delivered a record of $69.5 million." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "Our gross margin in Q3 '25 was at 37.3%. This quarter, it was 12.8%." and "in Q3, we generated roughly $8.9 million in gross profit." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "During Q3, Gorilla also deployed approximately $218 million of cash for property and equipment." and "we also closed the quarter with a little over $56 million, nearly $57 million of cash, while operating activities used about $30 million." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "At the end of September, our combined receivables and contract assets approximately stood at $203 million." and "we reduced our unbilled contract assets by over 50% from approximately $104 million plus to $52 million." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

Q&A

  • Gary Mobley, StoneX Group Inc.: asked about "the proposed acquisition of U.S.-based data center assets" and diligence status; CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan: "as and when our review is complete, we will communicate any material decisions through a formal announcement at that appropriate time."

  • Gary Mobley, StoneX Group Inc.: asked how much of 2027 targets are supported by current deployments and financing sources; CFO Bower: "that $6.6 million a month that we expect to be billing in the first quarter of 2027" and "we are doing with a Tier 1 investment bank a $1.7 billion bond... to refinance Yotta 1... and then... finalize the financing for Yotta 2."

  • Brian Kinstlinger, Alliance Global Partners: asked remaining CapEx and Yotta timelines; CFO Bower: "it's $100 million on Yotta 1" and "to 2, it's $1.5 billion"; CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan: "we will be at full capacity on Yotta 1 by the January of next year" and "Yotta 2... there will be a full deployment by February."

  • Fedor Shabalin, B. Riley Securities: pressed on convertible repayment and dilution; CFO Bower: "we drew down $25 million" and "we have to repay the face value, which is $27.75 million" and "upon effectiveness, we will be able to pay it off"; CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan: "our intention... is to repay the outstanding obligation in cash over the next 4 to 5 weeks" and "our aim is to pursue a resolution that minimizes further equity dilution."

  • Michael Donovan, Compass Point: asked Korat cost and timing; CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan: "Our cost per build is between USD 4 million and USD 4.5 million per megawatt" and "we are able to finish the construction from time of build in a span of 6 to 9 months"; CFO Bower: "to get from land acquisition all the way to site ready for building will be about $14 million, $15 million all in."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative to neutral on financing/regulatory uncertainty, with direct downside framing such as "plan B" if "the $1.7 billion bond financing... does not go through" (Bharath Nagaraj, Cantor Fitzgerald & Co.) and concerns about "the share price" and acquisition timing (Fedor Shabalin, B. Riley Securities).

  • Management: slightly positive but defensive on execution/stock pressure, including "Our share price has taken a dip" (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan) and confidence language like "we are very confident" (CFO Bower) alongside hedges such as "subject to market conditions and final documentation" (CFO Bower).

  • Versus last quarter: the tone added more explicit external constraints, with Q3 emphasizing "additional controls affecting the advanced chip exports" (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan), while Q2 leaned more heavily on ramp optimism like "Gorilla is in hyper growth mode" (CFO Bower).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance framing stayed consistent, with Q3 reiterating "minimum revenue outlook for 2026 remains at $200 million" and "2027 revenue target remains at $450 million to $500 million" (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan) versus Q2 stating "our revenue outlook for 2026 now stands at least $200 million" and "we're targeting revenues of about $450 million to $500 million" (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan).

  • The operational discussion shifted from deployment progress in Q2 ("the equipment deliveries are underway and deployment have commenced" for Yotta Phase 1) to commissioning lifecycle clarity in Q3: "A server delivered is not necessarily a server commissioned... accepted... generating cash." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • Financing detail increased in Q3, with CFO Bower describing "a $1.7 billion bond" timeline, while Q2 referenced project finance more generally: "we intend to fund the balance of the payments from a larger project finance facility." (CFO Bower)

Risks and Concerns

  • "The U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security has announced additional controls affecting the advanced chip exports and certain remote access arrangements involving overseas data centers." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "Capital expenditure is not automatically value creation." and "a data center... without customers paying is merely very expensive lighting installation." (CEO & Executive Chairman Chandan)

  • "The markets overall have been -- there's no secret, they've been a bit tumultuous in the past weeks." and the $1.7B financing was noted as "subject to market conditions and final documentation." (CFO Bower)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a record revenue quarter and reaffirmed its $200 million minimum 2026 revenue outlook and $450 million to $500 million 2027 revenue target, while focusing investor attention on commissioning and billing milestones at Yotta, near-term project financing execution including the proposed $1.7 billion bond, regulatory compliance under updated U.S. export controls, and accelerating conversion of receivables into cash alongside efforts to limit dilution from the $27.75 million note repayment plan.

data.title: Alibaba reportedly sued over Megaspeed ties amid Nvidia spy scandal
data.description:
Alibaba (BABA) is said to have been sued by shareholders in New York on Thursday, with investors alleging that the Chinese e-commerce giant misled them by concealing its connections to a suspected Chinese spy whose links to former Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang reportedly contributed to his resignation last week.

According to a ​proposed class action filed in Manhattan federal court, Alibaba inflated its share price by knowingly ​and materially understating in its 2024, 2025, and 2026 annual reports the risks that ⁠actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business, Reuters reported.

Shareholders cited Alibaba's relationship with Megaspeed, a ​Singaporean company suspected of helping Beijing gain access to advanced Nvidia AI chips, and whose executive Alice Huang ​had a relationship with Jensen Huang, who is not related to her.

The shareholders said Alibaba shares fell 14% over four days last week because of media reports on Alibaba's ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, including that Alibaba had ​become Megaspeed's “dominant” customer, the report said. 

Nvidia itself faces several shareholder lawsuits over the spy scandal, including allegations of lax oversight by its directors.

The e-commerce giant's CEO Eddie Wu said on Thursday that Alibaba remained on track for $100B in external cloud revenue and a 20% EBITDA margin by 2030, despite U.S. curbs on ​access to computing power that ​could affect the company's ⁠products and services next year. The restrictions were imposed after Huang resigned from Nvidia.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, along with ​her husband and sister, built a network of companies across ⁠China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, The Information has reported previously.

When orders for Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export restrictions  stalled, Alice Huang used ties to Nvidia to secure supplies, helping move about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China, according to the report. Some chips ultimately served Alibaba (BABA), Tencent (TCEHY), and smaller Chinese AI labs.

data.title: CVR Energy prices $1.25B of 9.250% senior secured notes due 2032
data.description:
• US refiner CVR Energy (CVI) said Thursday that it has priced its previously announced private placement of $1.25B in aggregate principal amount of 9.250% senior secured notes due 2032.
  • The notes will be issued at 98.980% of their principal value and will mature on March 15, 2032. The offering is expected to close on November 25, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
  • Before the closing of the acquisition, the notes will be secured solely by a first-priority interest in an escrow account and its funds, without guarantees. 
  • The stock has risen 33% so far this year.

data.title: Elastic outlines FY 2027 revenue of $2.0B-$2.008B while raising non-GAAP operating margin guide to ~19.5%
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Elastic (ESTC) Q2 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • "We are pleased to report another solid quarter of sales execution, enabling us to beat across all guided metrics and to deliver on our acceleration path." (CEO & Executive Director Ashutosh Kulkarni)
  • "Q2 total revenue was $496 million, growing 17%. Sales-led subscription revenue grew 19% to $415 million, and we delivered a non-GAAP operating margin of 22.2%, a record for the company." (CEO Kulkarni)
  • "We also announced the acquisition of HoneyHive today, an emerging leader in agent observability and evaluations." (CEO Kulkarni)
  • "While we believe HoneyHive will contribute to revenue growth over the long term, we do not expect material revenue contribution from the acquisition in FY '27." (Chief Financial Officer Navam Welihinda)
  • "I'm also pleased to report that Elastic achieved GAAP operating margin profitability this quarter." (CFO Welihinda)

Outlook

  • "For the third quarter of fiscal '27, we expect total revenue in the range of $507.5 million to $508.5 million" and "sales-led subscription revenue in the range of $432 million to $433 million." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "We expect non-GAAP operating margin for the third quarter to be approximately 21%" and "non-GAAP diluted earnings per share in the range of $0.90 to $0.92." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "For FY '27, we expect total revenue in the range of $2 billion to $2.008 billion" and "sales-led subscription revenue in the range of $1.682 billion to $1.690 billion." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "We are raising our non-GAAP operating margin guide to be approximately 19.5%" and "non-GAAP diluted earnings per share in the range of $3.35 to $3.41." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "During our last guidance, we anticipated FX rates of 1.17 against the euro and 1.36 against the pound" and "the stronger dollar is expected to create a total headwind of $9.5 million in the back half of the year." (CFO Welihinda)

Financial Results

  • "Our cRPO in the second quarter was $1.157 billion" and "our RPO for the second quarter was $1.858 billion." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "We delivered subscription gross margins of 82%, total gross margins of 78% and an operating margin of 22.2%, exceeding our guidance from last quarter." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "We achieved an adjusted free cash flow margin of approximately 9%" and "we continue to expect 21.5% adjusted free cash flow margin for the year." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "During the second quarter, we returned approximately $55 million to shareholders" and "the Board has authorized another $500 million for share buybacks." (CFO Welihinda)

Q&A

  • Brian Essex, JPMorgan: asked how outages, vulnerabilities, and network degradation are changing customer conversations across security and observability; CEO Kulkarni: "we are seeing a definite increase in the number of conversations that we are having on security" and "I expect this to be a continued tailwind for our business."
  • Brian Essex, JPMorgan: asked what is embedded in 2H assumptions; CFO Welihinda: "the euro and the pound have really substantially weakened" and "Q4 is about 20% higher than Q3 from a self-managed base perspective" plus "we're just being generally cautious about those regions."
  • Matthew Hedberg, RBC: asked medium-term impact of HoneyHive beyond FY '27; CEO Kulkarni: "it's a very strategic acquisition" and "in the medium term, it is definitely going to really give us some tailwinds."
  • Raimo Lenschow, Barclays: asked how observability product expansion (including metrics) changes competitive positioning; CEO Kulkarni: "metrics is the area that we've talked to you in the past about" and "we believe is definitely going to allow us to bring our observability rates back up."
  • Matthew Martino, Goldman Sachs: asked whether the “sole enterprise SIEM” win signals broader consolidation opportunity; CEO Kulkarni: "we have been taking share from incumbents" and said Elastic’s advantage is in "very, very complex" environments.
  • Tyler Radke, Citi: asked how agentic products could change consumption; CEO Kulkarni: "the primary and largest part of consumption is compute consumption" and "you are going to see more and more token consumption come through the Elastic platform."
  • Koji Ikeda, BofA: asked what could drive sales-led growth sustainably over 20% if cRPO stays near 20%; CFO Welihinda: "you have new and expansions and renewals that happen on the tail end" and "we are targeting greater than 20% in fiscal 2029."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive, emphasizing acceleration and probing durability, with recurring checks on second-half assumptions, Europe/Middle East caution, and the self-managed renewal shape, including "what is the risk of self-managed deal push-outs in Q4?" (Howard Ma, Guggenheim)
  • Management’s prepared-remarks tone was positive and execution-focused, anchored by profitability and product cadence, including "another solid quarter of sales execution" (CEO Kulkarni) and "Sustainable GAAP profitability is a significant milestone" (CFO Welihinda)
  • In Q&A, management was confident on demand/consumption but more cautious on macro/FX, including "we just took a big hit on FX" and "we're just going to be generally cautious about those regions" (CFO Welihinda)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • "Q2 was a strong quarter for Elastic" and "Total revenue and sales-led subscription revenue growth both accelerated from Q1" while "we saw emerging FX headwinds in Europe." (CFO Welihinda)
  • Compared with Q1’s emphasis on "we also acquired Deductive AI" and a board transition, Q2 added a second AI-focused acquisition with "the acquisition of HoneyHive" and introduced new agentic launches, including "Elastic AlertZero" and "Elastic Nightshift." (CEO Kulkarni)
  • Q1 guidance highlighted "we expect total revenue and sales-led subscription revenue growth to accelerate in the second half"; Q2 reiterated the shape but tied it more explicitly to "one renewal timing factor" and quantified the FX impact as "a total headwind of $9.5 million." (CFO Welihinda)

Risks and Concerns

  • "We saw emerging FX headwinds in Europe" and "the stronger dollar is expected to create a total headwind of $9.5 million in the back half of the year." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "Given on what's going on geopolitically in the Middle East and with FX in Europe, we're just being generally cautious about those regions." (CFO Welihinda)
  • "One renewal timing factor explains much of the shape of the second half" tied to "self-managed renewals" with a base "weighted 20% more towards Q4." (CFO Welihinda)

Final Takeaway

Elastic’s management described Q2 as a quarter of accelerating revenue and sales-led subscription growth, record non-GAAP operating margin, and a milestone shift to what the CFO called "sustainable GAAP operating margin profitability." Leadership tied momentum to Security and Search strength, rising AI adoption among large customers, and a faster product cadence with agentic releases (AlertZero, Nightshift, and Context Engine), while acknowledging near-term headwinds from FX and a more cautious stance on parts of Europe and the Middle East. The company also highlighted capital returns through an expanded $500 million buyback authorization and signaled a forthcoming shift in revenue disclosures starting in FY 2028 to emphasize sales-led subscription revenue, self-serve subscription revenue, and professional services.

data.title: Webull outlines $90T perps opportunity as crypto perpetuals go live
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Webull (BULL) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "I am proud to announce Webull delivered record results in the third quarter with client assets exceeding $32 billion, revenue reaching $219 million, up 39% year-over-year, and adjusted operating profit of $70 million, up 91% year-over-year." (President & Director Anthony Michael Denier)
  • Denier tied engagement to regulatory and product catalysts, saying the June pattern day trader change "has been a significant tailwind" and that Webull "recently announced our intention to launch" perpetual futures "by the end of this month" while also stating, "perps trading has gone live as of the start of this call today." (President & Director Denier)
  • Denier highlighted strategic actions across pillars, including "a strategic partnership with X, through which Webull will serve as a Cashtag partner," the completion of the Pi Securities acquisition in Thailand, and institutional momentum via Meritz Securities’ MOUM app launch. (President & Director Denier)
  • "Total quarterly revenue reached $219 million" and "adjusted operating profit reached $70 million, representing an adjusted operating margin of 32%." (CFO & Director H. Wang)
  • Wang added that the company’s options business "is now among the top 5 in the U.S. by market share, having exceeded 6% of the U.S. options market for the first time." (CFO & Director Wang)

Outlook

  • Management did not provide formal revenue or EPS guidance in the prepared remarks or Q&A in this transcript.
  • Denier framed near-term trading activity sensitivity to market conditions, saying elevated volatility can lift volumes early but warning, "if this volatility continues longer, we could see some retail weakness." (President & Director Denier)
  • On marketing posture, Wang said the company generally targets "marketing expense as a percentage of revenue of between 20% to 30%" and added, "in Q4, you'll probably see a little bit of pickup, but not significantly," while also noting Pi Securities will be consolidated for a full quarter in Q4. (CFO & Director Wang)

Financial Results

  • Webull reported "record total revenue of $219 million" and "adjusted operating expenses" of "$149 million," alongside "adjusted operating profit of $70 million" and "adjusted net income" of "$58 million." (President & Director Anthony Michael Denier; CFO & Director H. Wang)
  • Trading-related revenue was "$165 million," while interest-related revenue was "$43 million," which Wang said was "flat year-over-year" as "the increase in margin financing revenue" was "offset by a decline in stock lending." (CFO & Director Wang)
  • Activity metrics included "DARTs" of "approximately 1.8 million" and options DARTs of "approximately 628,000." (CFO & Director Wang)
  • Client assets reached "$32.4 billion"; Denier said that excluding "approximately $3 billion attributable to the Pi Securities acquisition," client assets were "approximately $29.4 billion." (President & Director Denier)

Q&A

  • Edward Engel, Compass Point: asked about "the health of the retail trader" and what drove October outperformance; President Denier replied, "overall, we are seeing healthy activity" but added, "I am really concerned if this volatility continues longer," and said October strength included brand awareness and organic wins from "power users or large options traders."
  • Elias Abboud, BofA Securities: asked about agentic trading uptake and volume; President Denier said, "as of today, we do not currently have on-platform agents" and described increasing third-party MCP activity, adding that non-U.S. markets "Japan, Malaysia, Hong Kong" were "really outperforming with agentic trading."
  • Abboud, BofA Securities: asked about perpetuals roadmap and economics; President Denier said, "the economics on perps are actually much more favorable," confirmed production launch of perpetual crypto trading, and cited scale, saying, "perps were a $90 trillion market by volume in 2025."
  • Mike Grondahl, Northland: asked about Meritz rollout and marketing spend; President Denier said Meritz volumes were growing "about 5% to 8%" month-over-month and that institutional flow was "almost 1/5 of our total order flow"; CFO Wang said Q4 marketing should "pick up" modestly, with 2025 promotion amortization "almost completely" rolling off by 2027.
  • Grondahl, Northland: asked for prediction markets or crypto revenue breakouts; CFO Wang answered, "we did not separately break out prediction markets" and President Denier added spot crypto trading was "pretty flat" while crypto prediction contracts saw "huge uplift" and that Q2-to-Q3 prediction market volumes were up "another 26%" quarter-over-quarter.
  • Lance Jessurun, Scotiabank: asked about capital return and buybacks; CFO Wang prioritized balance sheet needs, growth capital, and M&A, then said for excess cash, "if the stock price is attractive... we'll definitely be looking" at repurchases; President Denier added, "we're in a blackout period."
  • Jessurun, Scotiabank: asked about Pi’s September contribution and whether the "70,000" accounts were included; CFO Wang said Pi revenue was "just under $4 million," said Pi "is profitable," and confirmed the accounts were included.
  • Christopher Brendler, Rosenblatt: asked about marketing priorities under the new U.S. CMO and the House Select Committee report impact; President Denier said U.S. marketing will include "brand" while "the best money spent will actually be outside the U.S.," and stated that after the report, the company saw "the largest amount of incoming net deposits we've ever seen the week the report came out" and was "probably down about $80 million in customer AUM" over the 10 days following.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and expansion-oriented, focused on durability and monetization of new initiatives, including "agentic trading" and "perpetuals" (Abboud, BofA Securities) and capital return (Jessurun, Scotiabank).
  • Management’s tone in prepared remarks was positive and assertive, anchored by "record results" and operating leverage, while in Q&A Denier was more conditional on macro, saying, "I am really concerned if this volatility continues longer." (President & Director Denier)
  • Versus Q2, management language shifted from early confirmation of the PDT uplift to greater emphasis on sustaining share gains and navigating scrutiny; Denier referenced "headline headwinds" and framed October as a counter-narrative: "our volumes exploded." (President & Director Denier)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized post-PDT sustainability with five months of data and highlighted options market share "exceeded 6%"; Q2 centered on initial execution after June 4 and described PDT as the "defining event for the quarter." (CFO & Director Wang; President & Director Anthony Michael Denier)
  • Strategic focus broadened in Q3 with Pi closing (vs. Q2 expecting it to close) and with new launches/announcements including MiCAR approval in Europe, Italy market entry, the X Cashtag partnership, and perpetual futures going live. (President & Director Denier)
  • Analysts’ focus shifted from PDT mechanics and early AI differentiation in Q2 to Q3 questions on agentic trading uptake, perps economics, capital return, and Pi integration contribution.

Risks and Concerns

  • Denier addressed U.S. political and regulatory scrutiny, stating, "the matters raised in the Select Committee's report are not new" and emphasizing, "U.S. customer data is stored in the United States" and "Our employees in China do not have access to sensitive U.S. customer information." (President & Director Denier)
  • Denier cited a market-risk dynamic for retail activity: "for the first kind of 3 months with elevated volatility" volumes can rise, but "Once we start getting to 6 months, you start seeing it really slow down." (President & Director Denier)
  • Wang framed capital needs as a constraint on buybacks, pointing to broker-dealer capital requirements and saying, "We need to have capital to finance the growing margin book." (CFO & Director Wang)

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 as a record quarter driven by sustained post-PDT engagement and higher options activity, while expanding product breadth with prediction markets, nano futures, and the launch of crypto perpetuals. Executives highlighted the Pi Securities acquisition as an immediate scale step in APAC and positioned institutional growth through partners like Meritz, while also addressing House Select Committee headlines by reiterating prior disclosures and U.S.-based custody and data controls. Marketing plans were framed around brand in the U.S. and growth internationally, with management signaling a modest Q4 marketing pickup and continued focus on operating leverage.

data.title: Ross Stores forecasts Q4 comp 4%-5% and FY2026 EPS $8.75-$8.84 as it cites sustained traffic gains
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Ross Stores (ROST) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "We delivered a very strong quarter from both a top and bottom line perspective." (CEO & Director James Conroy)
  • "Total sales were up 12%, driven by a robust 8% increase in comparable store sales." (CEO Conroy)
  • "Customer traffic remained the primary driver of our strong comparable store sales growth." (CEO Conroy)
  • "In the third quarter, cosmetics and home were our strongest businesses." (CEO Conroy)
  • "Consolidated inventories at quarter end increased 13%, in line with the growth in total sales." (CEO Conroy)
  • "These openings completed our 2026 store growth program, reflecting 89 Ross and 26 dd's DISCOUNTS openings or 115 new locations in total, which is 5 more than our original plan at the outset of the year." (CEO Conroy)
  • "Total sales for the period grew 12% to $6.3 billion with comparable store sales increasing 8%." (Executive VP & CFO William Sheehan)
  • "Third quarter operating margin increased 70 basis points to 12.3% compared to 11.6% last year." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "Third quarter net income was $606 million compared to $512 million last year, and earnings per share were $1.91 compared to $1.58 in the prior year." (CFO Sheehan)

Outlook

  • "Comparable store sales are forecasted to increase 4% to 5%, with earnings per share expected to be in the range of $2.16 to $2.25 versus $2 last year." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "Our guidance assumptions for the fourth quarter of 2026 reflect total sales are forecast to increase 7% to 9% versus the prior year." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "If same-store sales perform in line with our forecast, operating margin for the fourth quarter is planned to be in the range of 12.1% to 12.4% compared to 12.3% last year." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "For the full year of 2026, our updated guidance for earnings per share is $8.75 to $8.84." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "We are confident in our plans for the upcoming holiday season and are maintaining our sales outlook for the fourth quarter." (CFO Sheehan)
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s full-year EPS outlook of $8.61 to $8.77, management updated it to $8.75 to $8.84. "As a reminder, this guidance includes an approximate $0.60 earnings per share benefit from tariff refunds recognized in the second quarter." (CFO Sheehan)

Financial Results

  • "Gross margin for the third quarter improved by 70 basis points." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "Merchandise margin rose 20 basis points as the strong buying environment and the benefits of lapping tariff-related costs were partially offset by planned higher shrink as we cycled last year's favorable results." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "Partially offsetting these benefits were higher freight costs, which deleveraged by 25 basis points from higher fuel prices." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "As noted in today's release, we repurchased approximately 1.4 million shares during the quarter for an aggregate total cost of $319 million" and "we remain on track to buy back a total of $1.275 billion in stock during 2026." (CFO Sheehan)
  • "The company's Board of Directors declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.445 per share." (CFO Sheehan)

Q&A

  • Matthew Boss, JPMorgan: asked about the two-year stack acceleration and durability; CEO Conroy: "our first proof point of can you comp the comp should be a resounding yes" and said multiple initiatives are "very, very early" in marketing, merchandising, and store labor reallocation.
  • Lorraine Maikis, BofA: asked about Q4 investment levels and 2027; CEO Conroy: "In the fourth quarter, we're ticking up slightly in marketing" and "making some investments in store labor," while adding, "it's much too early" for 2027 guidance.
  • Michael Binetti, Evercore ISI: questioned implied two-year stack deceleration and the "long-term algorithm" reference; CEO Conroy: "I wouldn't read anything into" a 2-year stack moving from 15% to a 14% guide; Group President, COO & Director Michael Hartshorn: "we haven't changed our long-term algorithm, which is calling for 5% unit growth, 3% to 4% comp, and double-digit EPS growth."
  • Brooke Roach, Goldman Sachs: asked about freight/fuel inflation and operating margin ceiling; COO Hartshorn: "a lot of what's driving the freight inflation right now is fuel" and "we would find other opportunities in the business."
  • Corey Tarlowe, Jefferies: asked what refined Q4 EPS; CFO Sheehan: "that reflects higher fuel costs relative to our initial guidance" and "we expect kind of SG&A to delever a bit" due to "modestly higher store payroll and marketing"; Tarlowe also asked about pricing pressure; CEO Conroy: "I don't think we've seen any competitive pressure from a pricing standpoint that's been hurting our business."
  • Simeon Siegel, Guggenheim: asked about vendors/AUR and competitive landscape; CEO Conroy: "off-price is still a share gainer" and the comp was "mostly transactions" with only "a small portion" from basket/AUR.
  • Mark Altschwager, Baird: asked about merchandise margin drivers and shrink; CFO Sheehan: "the buying environment has been great"; COO Hartshorn: "The total cost of shrink in the company has been relatively flat"; Altschwager also asked about retention; CEO Conroy: "I don't have a specific metric to share."
  • Charles Grom, Gordon Haskett: asked about consumer crosscurrents and weather; CEO Conroy: "The tail end of October... was very rough weather" and said Q4 saw "a really, really nice step-up back to kind of in line with our guidance."
  • Dana Telsey, Telsey Advisory Group: asked about regional performance and Northeast; COO Hartshorn: "All regions had a solid mid-single-digit comp growth or better" and "as a group have significantly exceeded our pro forma estimates" in the Northeast.
  • Irwin Boruchow, Wells Fargo: asked about shrink headwind; COO Hartshorn: "the unfavorability this year was only that comparison" and, on go-forward: "No, it's not."
  • Jay Sole, UBS: pressed on whether the strategy implies going upmarket and how to add "better" brands without raising AUR; CEO Conroy: "We absolutely don't want to abandon the core modest income customer" and said the basket was "only up modestly" while keeping AUR low.
  • Aneesha Sherman, Bernstein: asked if inventory is still a lever and about weekly cadence; CEO Conroy: "Our inventory is up 13%. Our sales for the quarter were up 12%" and said the fourth week of October "was a difficult week" but recent trends were in line with Q4 guidance.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly positive, with repeated durability-testing on "comping the comp," margin/freight sensitivity, shrink quality, and whether investments or pricing are masking demand; questions like "is there something... we should think about" (Evercore ISI Binetti) and "A lot of crosscurrents" (Gordon Haskett Grom) signaled ongoing skepticism despite strong results.
  • Management: positive and confident, repeatedly emphasizing durability and early-innings opportunity, including "a resounding yes" on sustaining comps (CEO Conroy) and "we haven't changed our long-term algorithm" (COO Hartshorn).
  • Versus last quarter: management kept the same core message around a transactions-led comp and early-stage initiatives, while analysts continued to probe sustainability; this quarter added more pointed cost questioning around fuel/freight and more detailed scrutiny of shrink and weekly weather impacts.

Quarter-over-quarter Comparison

  • Current quarter: management highlighted Q3 as "a very strong quarter" with comps driven by transactions and called out weather pressure late in the quarter; "unseasonably warm weather dampened fall selling late in the quarter." (CEO Conroy)
  • Prior quarter: the company emphasized tariff refunds as a major factor in Q2 margin and earnings; "Gross margin improved by 625 basis points, driven primarily by 405 basis points of tariff refunds." (CFO Sheehan, prior transcript)
  • Guidance trajectory: in Q2, management said it was "raising our outlook for both the third and fourth quarters" (CFO Sheehan, prior transcript); in Q3, management said it was "maintaining our sales outlook for the fourth quarter" while updating full-year EPS to $8.75 to $8.84. (CFO Sheehan)
  • Strategic focus: both quarters emphasized the same flywheel pillars—marketing modernization, vendor access, and store experience—while Q3 added store growth completion detail and cited newer markets "including the Northeast" as "significantly exceed[ing] our expectations." (CEO Conroy)

Risks and Concerns

  • "Unseasonably warm weather dampened fall selling late in the quarter." (CEO Conroy)
  • "Higher freight costs... deleveraged by 25 basis points from higher fuel prices." (CFO Sheehan)
  • Management cited shrink volatility in comparisons rather than an underlying increase: "last year, we had a favorable true-up" and "the total cost of shrink... has been relatively flat." (COO Hartshorn)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as a transactions-led, broad-based comp performance with expanding operating margin, supported by what it described as early-stage improvements in marketing, merchandising, and store execution. For Q4, management maintained its sales outlook while guiding to a 4% to 5% comp and EPS of $2.16 to $2.25, alongside a full-year EPS range of $8.75 to $8.84 that includes an approximate $0.60 benefit from tariff refunds recognized earlier in the year; executives also flagged fuel-driven freight pressure and weather volatility as key near-term variables heading into the holidays.

data.title: Nvidia in advanced talks to buy diffusion AI startup Inception for over $500M - report
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) is in advanced talks to acquire Inception, a two-year-old AI startup developing diffusion-based large language models, in a deal valued at more than $500M, according to a report by The Information.

The deal would bring Inception's three co-founders—Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, and Volodymyr Kuleshov—into Nvidia full-time. The proposed transaction would also include additional earnout awards for Inception employees, contingent on meeting specified performance targets, the report said, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Founded about two years ago, Inception is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with more than 30 employees. It previously raised $50M from investors, including Menlo Ventures, M12, Mayfield, and Nvidia (NVDA).

The startup develops diffusion-based large language models designed to generate text faster than conventional models. Its Mercury family of models uses an iterative refinement process to generate multiple tokens in parallel rather than sequentially, potentially accelerating text generation. Inception says its Mercury models can generate text up to 10 times faster than comparable models. The company has also developed diffusion-based models for coding and published research on multimodal understanding and reasoning.

Nvidia's (NVDA) discussions with Inception began before the departure of CEO Jensen Huang and followed interest in a similar transaction from Microsoft (MSFT), the report added.

The acquisition would strengthen Nvidia's (NVDA) efforts to develop its own AI models and expand its Nemotron portfolio of open models, which businesses and government customers can customize for specific applications. Nemotron models are already used by Booz Allen Hamilton (BAH), Palantir Technologies (PLTR), and several U.S. government agencies.

Inception's researchers are also expected to apply their diffusion technology to physical AI models used in robotics, another potential area of development for Nvidia (NVDA), the report said.

Nvidia (NVDA) did not immediately respond to Seeking Alpha's request for comment.
